problem: Decision D31 adds one artifact kind and four story keys that the shipped registry does not hold. Until it does, a flag record under .factory/stories/flags/ matches no kind and is blocked by [_unknown]; a story that carries flag, flag_change, flag_exempt or flag_irreversible fails its frontmatter check; a toolchain file with a [flags] table is outside the [toolchain] row's description and over its cap; and the [deferred-item] row names the defer skill as the only writer, although the checkpoint must write one item, deferred/flag-<stem>.md, for each live temporary flag. The [flag] row also needs two things the registry's format lacks: a stem cell, because a record's path is its key percent-encoded and so the id no longer equals the file stem; and the lock value removed.
proposed_resolution: Add the [flag] row and [flag.frontmatter] exactly as rewrite/spec/artifacts/flag.md gives them, with the stem cell and its check, the lock value removed and the keys permanent_because, default_because and repo, and with the skeleton templates/flag.md. Add four optional keys to [story.frontmatter]: flag = "str?", flag_change (enable, remove or withdraw), flag_exempt = "str?" and flag_irreversible = "str?". Name the [flags] table in the [toolchain] row and raise that row's cap to 12,000 bytes. Add vsdd checkpoint to the [deferred-item] writer. Extend the pins in tests/unit/test_policy.py. Then shrink rewrite/spec/artifacts/flag.md to a pointer at the shipped row. D31R-F-15 names the same format additions; one change closes both.

problem: [reveals] must hold one entry per artifact kind (lint L-POLICY), and a kind with no entry is treated as revealing every walled class, so `vsdd list flag` would be refused for every walled caller. Three writer texts in classes.toml also become incomplete. The survey writes the table [flags.approved] of factory.toml, and no key of [flags], which stays a person's (check F-FILL, rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml; rewrite/spec/config/flags.md). The survey writes the inherited flag records into the stories class. The checkpoint writes one deferred item for each live temporary flag.
proposed_resolution: Add "list flag" = ["stories"] to [reveals]. Widen the three writer texts: [config] names the survey as the writer of [flags.approved] only; [stories] names the survey for inherited flag records; [deferred] names vsdd checkpoint. No class, no wall row and no grant is added or changed: flag records live in the stories class on purpose (rewrite/spec/artifacts/flag.md).

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/config.py and next/tests/unit/test_config.py (the shipped loader); rewrite/spec/tables/config-keys.toml; rewrite/spec/schemas/config.schema.json; the annotated example in rewrite/spec/topics/project-configuration.md
problem: The configuration key list exists in four places that must gain the flag keys together, and none has them: the shipped loader rejects [flags] as an unknown section, and config-keys.toml (15.7 KB) and config.schema.json (14.7 KB) are both too close to the 16 KB file limit to take the rows as they are. The rows are held meanwhile in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-config-keys.toml. The keys live in two tables of factory.toml: [flags], which a person writes, and [flags.approved], which only the survey writes (rewrite/spec/config/flags.md). A [[repo]] entry may carry a flags table as well.
proposed_resolution: Teach the loader both tables from the rows of rewrite/spec/tables/flag-config-keys.toml: types and defaults, the four values of flags.require, compiled patterns, repo.flags, and the meaning of set_by. A key marked person (flags.require) is accepted only in [flags]. A key marked proposal is accepted in [flags.approved]; one that also has override = true (flags.enabled among them) is accepted in [flags] too, where a person's value wins. Compute the three states off, requested and on from the two tables. Ship accept and reject cases; add the section to the annotated example; for the two files at the size limit either split them or have them name flag-config-keys.toml as the home of the flag rows. An invalid value must never switch a flag check off: while flags are on, a pattern that does not compile is a configuration error and the checks that need it fail with cannot measure. Four keys are valid when empty: key_env, key_patterns, definition_patterns and definitions_check (header of rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml).

problem: Decision D31 adds no decision kind but changes two rows the table does not yet show. Row spec: approving a specification whose toolchain file says enabled = true, when the decision would accept the decision record that flags.decision names, needs the value flags=<source> with that file's source, whichever of the four sources it is; flags=decline -- <words> is accepted instead where the source is existing; a flags value on any other approval is refused (F-APPROVE in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml; rewrite/spec/topics/flag-system-choice.md). Row merge: where flags.removal = human, the checkpoint of maintain opens one merge decision for each flag that is due for removal, with the id merge.flag-<stem>, before any cleanup story is written. No story and no pull request exist at that point, so the row's opened_when (a delivered story waits) and its note (approve performs the merge; reject closes the pull request and descopes the story) do not describe it, and its reject needs until=<yyyy-mm-dd> naming a day after today (F-APPROVE; F-REMOVE in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-release-checks.toml; rewrite/spec/topics/flag-lifecycle.md). A flag adds no wait at vsdd story deliver: a cleanup story merges as delivery.merge says, and where flags.removal = auto no decision is opened.
proposed_resolution: Row spec: write the approve choice as approve [variant=<id>] [topology=single or split] [flags=<source> | flags=decline -- <words>], with a note that a flags value is required exactly when the decision would accept the flag decision record, that it is stored in the decision's values, and that settling refuses it on any other approval. Row merge: add to opened_when that, where flags.removal = human, the maintain checkpoint opens merge.flag-<stem> for a flag that is due for removal, before a cleanup story is written; write the reject choice as reject [until=<yyyy-mm-dd>]; add to the note that for a removal decision approve lets the next maintain run write the cleanup story, and reject, which needs until, keeps the flag and makes it not due again before that day, with nothing merged, closed or descoped. The grammar of decide needs no change: flags and until are named values. Do not add a wait at story deliver, and do not open the decision when a person asked for the removal with a change request.

where: rewrite/spec/tables/lint-checks.toml; the lint suite under next/tests/lint/
problem: The flag duties of agents live in method files, and nothing yet checks that a method named in rewrite/spec/tables/flag-duties.toml carries its Feature flags section, so a duty could be dropped without any check failing.
proposed_resolution: Add the lint check L-FLAG: every method the duty table names has a section headed Feature flags; no other method has one; every agent the table names lists the method. Ship the duty table as data beside the roster so the lint reads one source.

problem: The identifier table lists every identifier scheme, and the flag key is a new one: it is the identifier of a flag record, its file stem is a function of it, and it is never reused. Test names carry a second function of it, the encoded form, which no two keys that tests can name may share.
proposed_resolution: Add a row for the flag key: any key existing code reads, held to the tidy form ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ for a new flag; chosen by the story-writer; the file stem is the key with /, % and whitespace percent-encoded; never reused, because the record of a removed flag is kept. For the encoded form point at the header of rewrite/spec/tables/flag-checks.toml, which defines it; do not restate it.

problem: The registry's one-line summary of decisions.md still reads "The record of the adopted decisions D1 to D30, as decided." The file now also records D31, under a heading for decisions adopted after 2026-11-23. The workflow that wrote D31 was not allowed to edit registry.toml.
proposed_resolution: Change the summary to "The record of the adopted decisions, D1 to D31, as decided." and regenerate the briefs.

where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/story-unit.schema.json (the acs field); rewrite/spec/topics/verdicts.md (items to account for); rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml (F-ITEMS)
problem: F-ITEMS (rewrite/spec/tables/flag-story-checks.toml) adds four review items that are not acceptance criteria to the items a story's review must account for: flag-off:<key>, for a story behind a flag and for a story that turns one on; flag-removed:<key>; flag-system; and not-a-flag. The workflow script hands reviewers the unit's acs list, and the shipped schema describes acs as acceptance criteria only, so without a change the reviewers are never told of an item the tool's verdict then waits for, and the story cannot converge. These items differ from a criterion in three ways. Only checked counts for them: not_checkable leaves the item uncovered. flag-off and flag-removed are added again in a later review loop whose commits touch a file of class source or tests. And not-a-flag is known only once the green gate has run, because it is added when the green evidence lists a marked line, so it cannot come from a unit the survey built before that gate.
proposed_resolution: Have the survey and the admission commands append the items that the story's own keys decide (flag-off, flag-removed, flag-system) to the unit's acs, and widen the field's description to say so. Carry not-a-flag to the reviewers from the green gate's result, and have the tool's verdict add it from the green evidence. For a later loop, have the verdict and the script's list for that loop both carry flag-off or flag-removed when the loop's commits touch source or tests. Check that nothing reads every acs entry as AC-<N> (the criterion-to-test table is built from the red record's criteria map, not from acs); if a consumer does, carry the items in a field of their own and pass it in the review step's prompt instead. Prove with a harness scenario that a story behind a flag converges only when a reviewer marks flag-off checked, and that not_checkable does not converge it.
